Tracks: A — filing-index ingestion (known progression).

## Stages

- [ ] Stage 1: Local quarterly backfill to canonical Parquet
      Objective: Download a real archived quarter range from the SEC, keep the original bytes, and parse them into the canonical row contract, locally.
      Outcomes: O1, O3
      Consumes: the partner's SEC User-Agent identity and a chosen quarter range of at least one archived quarter
      Produces: a downloader with a single-process throttle at ≤3 req/s and an identifying User-Agent; SHA-256-addressed raw snapshots; a parser producing `sec-index-v1` rows; specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-spec-stage-1-findings.md
      Exit: O1: each quarter in the range is stored as validated original bytes with its SHA-256 and byte count. O3: Parquet rows matching the §4.5 row contract exist for that range, and malformed rows fail closed. The findings file records bytes, rows, elapsed time, peak memory and the observed request rate of the real run.
      Leaves out: source manifest (Stage 2); replay, generations and active pointer (Stage 3); reconciliation (Stage 4); shared lease budget (Stage 5); config validation and fixture coverage of the full range (Stage 6); Azure, traceability and observability (Stage 7); scheduling and deployment (Stage 8)
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 2: Daily discovery, catch-up and source manifest
      Objective: Discover and ingest daily indexes from `index.json` listings, with catch-up, through the same code path as backfill, and track each source's state durably.
      Outcomes: O2, O5
      Consumes: Stage 1's downloader, raw snapshots and parser
      Produces: the source, snapshot, workset-binding and processing records (§4.5 Source manifest); the `discover`/`collect`/`transform` commands shared by backfill and daily runs
      Exit: O2: a real catch-up from a past handoff date crosses a quarter boundary, reports `no_new_sources` and pending sources distinctly, and does not advance discovery past a failed listing. O5: backfill and daily runs call the same downloader and parser, with no per-mode copy.
      Leaves out: generations and pointer (Stage 3); lease budget (Stage 5); Azure storage of the manifest (Stage 7)
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 3: Replay and versioned quarter publication
      Objective: Rebuild from stored bytes without the SEC, and publish each quarter as an immutable generation behind a conditionally updated active pointer.
      Outcomes: O6, O9
      Consumes: Stage 2's manifest records and Stage 1's raw snapshots
      Produces: per-source observation output; the `publish` command; quarter generations with manifest.json, the active-pointer contract and the reader contract (§4.6)
      Exit: O6: a parser-version bump rebuilds output from raw storage with SEC access disabled, and the logical catalog is unchanged with no duplicates. O9: readers resolve every quarter through its pointer to an explicit file list, and the injected crash points in §6 Publication leave only complete generations visible.
      Leaves out: withdrawal gate (Stage 4); Table Storage and ADLS backends (Stage 7)
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 4: Reconciliation and gated withdrawals
      Objective: Re-read quarterly indexes, publish safe changes, and gate key removals behind hash-bound approval.
      Outcomes: O7, O10
      Consumes: Stage 3's generations, pointer and changes output
      Produces: the reconciliation workflow; `changes.parquet` per generation; withdrawal-approval records and the `awaiting_approval` state
      Exit: O7: a re-read records additions and field updates as a new generation, and unchanged hashes skip transformation. O10: absence from an open quarter withdraws nothing, a closed-quarter removal stays `awaiting_approval` until approval names its source hash, and stale daily replay cannot resurrect a withdrawn key.
      Leaves out: scheduled reconciliation runs (Stage 8)
      ROUTING: writing-plans

- [ ] Stage 5: One shared SEC request budget
      Objective: Make every collector (backfill, daily and reconciliation) take turns under one renewable lease and one request budget.
      Outcomes: O8
      Consumes: Stages 2 and 4's collectors
      Produces: the coordination lease and its namespace; daily-first turn order; halt-on-access-denied behavior
      Exit: O8: concurrent backfill, daily and reconciliation collectors never issue overlapping requests or exceed the configured rate including retries, and lease loss stops new requests (§6 Access).
      Leaves out: the Azure Storage lease backend (Stage 7)
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 6: Validated configuration, error outcomes and fixture coverage
      Objective: Validate every §4.8 setting before network I/O, map §5's named outcomes to exit codes, and complete golden fixtures for the chosen range.
      Outcomes: O11
      Consumes: Stages 1–5's commands
      Produces: `conf/sec-edgar-ingest.yaml` and its typed loader; the error-to-exit-code map; golden fixtures covering the historical formats in the chosen range (§4.6)
      Exit: O11: every §5 Configuration case is refused before external I/O, defaults load from config alone, and the §6 CI exit criteria pass on committed fixtures with no SEC download.
      Leaves out: deployment values for Azure (Stage 7)
      ROUTING: writing-plans

- [ ] Stage 7: Azure platform, traceability and smoke test
      Objective: Run the shared worker on Azure under ADF with managed identities, structured logs, run reports and alerts, with triggers disabled.
      Outcomes: O4
      Consumes: an accepted ADR and spec (§7 step 1); Stages 1–6
      Produces: `infra/azure/sec-edgar-ingest/` under version control; ADLS and Table Storage backends for the manifest, pointer and lease; attempt records and run reports (§4.5, §4.7); a pinned image digest
      Exit: O4: integration tests and fault injection pass in an isolated environment (§7 step 3), a bounded live smoke test and a raw-storage replay are recorded with their measured Azure cost (§7 steps 4–5), and approval and rollback are rehearsed.
      Leaves out: trigger enablement and runbooks (Stage 8)
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 8: Baseline and scheduled operation
      Objective: Run the production backfill and daily catch-up, reconcile once, then enable the triggers and accept scheduled runs on their evidence.
      Outcomes: O1, O2, O7 (in production)
      Consumes: Stage 7's deployed, reviewed image and configuration
      Produces: the release record (image digest, configuration revision, active generations); `docs/runbooks/` (§8); enabled daily and weekly triggers
      Exit: O1: every requested baseline unit is published, or the approved incomplete range is recorded. O2: daily ingestion is caught up from the handoff date and its trigger is enabled. O7: one manual reconciliation has run with gated candidates resolved, its weekly trigger is enabled, and observed scheduled runs match their reports (§7 steps 6–9).
      Leaves out: nothing
      ROUTING: writing-plans
